About the Opportunity 
 
 Founded in 1898, Northeastern is a global research university and the recognized leader in experience-driven lifelong learning. Our world-renowned experiential approach empowers our students, faculty, alumni, and partners to create impact far beyond the confines of discipline, degree, and campus.

 Our locations—in Arlington; Boston; Charlotte, North Carolina; London; Miami; New York City; Oakland; Portland, Maine; Seattle; Silicon Valley; Toronto; Vancouver; and the Massachusetts communities of Burlington and Nahant—are nodes in our growing global university system. Through this network, we expand opportunities for flexible, student-centered learning and collaborative, solutions-focused research.

 Northeastern’s comprehensive array of undergraduate and graduate programs— in a variety of on-campus and online formats—lead to degrees through the doctorate in nine colleges and schools. Among these, we offer more than 195 multi-discipline majors and degrees designed to prepare students for purposeful lives and careers.

 Northeastern University’s College of Engineering is a globally recognized leader in engineering education and research, distinguished by its interdisciplinary culture, strong industry partnerships, and commitment to translating fundamental discoveries into real-world impact. Located in Boston and supported by a global network of campuses and partners, the College brings together researchers across computer engineering, electrical engineering, mechanical engineering, civil engineering, robotics, artificial intelligence, materials, biotechnology, and other emerging fields.

 The Department of Electrical and Computer Engineering (ECE) at Northeastern University is a dynamic and rapidly growing academic community at the forefront of research and education in electrical engineering, computer engineering, and emerging computing technologies. The department brings together faculty with expertise spanning computer architecture and systems, artificial intelligence and machine learning, robotics, embedded and cyber-physical systems, communications and networking, signal processing, semiconductor and VLSI design, quantum computing, and emerging hardware technologies.

 Located in Boston, within one of the world’s leading technology and innovation ecosystems, Northeastern ECE offers exceptional opportunities for interdisciplinary collaboration across engineering, computer science, robotics, materials science, and the physical sciences. The department’s research is strongly connected to real-world applications through partnerships with industry, government, and leading research institutions, while Northeastern’s distinctive experiential-learning and cooperative education programs provide students with opportunities to connect classroom learning with cutting-edge engineering practice.
  
 About the Opportunity: 

 The Department of Electrical and Computer Engineering at Northeastern University is seeking outstanding candidates for Tenure-Track Faculty at the Assistant/Associate/Full Professor levels to strengthen the interdisciplinary thematic area of physical AI, embodied, wearable and assistive AI, described more broadly below.  Candidates with expertise in AI, machine learning, multi-modal sensing and learning, computer vision, embodied AI, human-centric AI, explainable and interpretable AI, trustworthy AI, AI on edge devices, physical intelligence, neuro-symbolic AI, AI reasoning are examples of areas that fit this theme.
     
 The university-wide Physical AI, Robotics & Autonomous Systems main theme brings together researchers working at the intersection of artificial intelligence, robotics, and the physical world to build systems that sense, reason, and act within real-world environments. This theme spans intelligent infrastructure and adaptive construction and manufacturing systems using digital twins and multi-agent controls; embodied and wearable AI systems that bridge HCI/design with rehabilitation and safe human-robot collaboration in clinical, home, community, and informal settings designed to support and empower the people they work alongside; automated self-driving laboratories that pair hardware instrumentation with active-learning machine learning to accelerate chemistry, materials, and biomanufacturing experimentation; AI-mediated telepresence enabling immersive, distance-spanning connection for shared environments to support creative collaboration; and telemedicine and physical AI systems for health that use autonomous modeling, monitoring, and digital-twin technologies to support translational and implementation health science. Spanning Boston and Charlotte, the theme draws on cross-college collaboration among COE (College of Engineering), CAMD (College of Arts, Media and Design), COS (College of Science), Khoury College of Computer Sciences, and Bouvé College of Health Sciences, together with Northeastern’s interdisciplinary ecosystem.  The theme is further strengthened by Northeastern's recently launched Physical AI Research (PAIR) Initiative, which advances the foundational science of Physical AI and fosters collaborations across strategic application domains, and by the Institute for Experiential Robotics (IER).

 Appointment will be primarily or fully in the Department of Electrical and Computer Engineering (ECE) within Northeastern University’s College of Engineering, with opportunities for joint cross-college appointments with the Khoury College of Computer Sciences, the College of Arts, Media and Design, or the Bouvé College of Health Sciences. The position will be based on Northeastern University’s Boston campus.

 Candidates with interest in joint appointments with other departments or colleges should indicate their intent in their application materials in the cover letter.

 Our tenure and promotion process values collaborative research and teamwork. Hires will be mentored for success, with mentoring teams and group guidance. In addition, a strong and effective faculty development strategy is part of the Northeastern institutional mission. The ADVANCE Office of Faculty Development office works in conjunction with the Office of Research Development (ORD), the Office of Belonging, the Center for Advancing Teaching and Learning Through Research (CATLR), and University Decision Support (UDS) to provide programs and trainings to further develop and support a thriving faculty.

 Responsibilities: 

 Responsibilities will include teaching undergraduate and graduate courses, lead an independent and externally funded research program, and participate in departmental, college, and university service. Qualified candidates must be prepared to work with global student populations.

 Qualifications:   

 A Ph.D., or foreign equivalent, in Electrical & Computer Engineering, Computer Science, Math, Physics, or closely related fields  by the employment start date.

 Senior-level candidates at the Associate and Full Professor levels should have a demonstrated record of developing transformative solutions to global challenges, sustaining a research program with a strong emphasis on interdisciplinary and translational research, teaching both undergraduate and graduate classes, and being an active, recognized leader nationally and internationally in their discipline.

 Applicants at the Associate level should have at least 4 years of academic or equivalent experience (e.g., industry, research) and at the Full Professor level at least 8 years or equivalent experience (e.g., industry, research).

 How to apply: Interested candidates should apply using the Northeastern University website. Applications must include the following, for further information on the statements, please see below.

 Cover letter – may identify a department of interest for a joint appointment within the College of Engineering or other colleges
 Full curriculum vita that includes a list of publications
 Statement of Research Interests, Objectives & Vision
 Statement of Teaching Interests & Philosophy
 Leadership statement
 Names and contact information for at least three professional references from whom letters of reference can be solicited as needed
 
 Applications will be reviewed on a rolling basis, as they arrive. The review is expected to start immediately and will continue until the position is filled.

 Successful faculty at Northeastern will be dynamic and innovative scholars with a record of research and teaching excellence and a commitment to fostering belonging in the university community.  Thus, strong candidates for this faculty position will have the expertise, knowledge, and skills to build their research, pedagogy, and curriculum in ways that reflect and enhance this commitment. Please indicate how your expertise, knowledge, and skills have prepared you to contribute to this work with written statements addressing the following prompts:
  
 Research statement (no longer than 5 pages): 
 Please describe the focus of your research, including the questions you have identified, the funding you have received to support the work (if applicable), the results you have discovered, and the products of these efforts. Highlight any cross-disciplinary research efforts you have undertaken. Please also describe any research you have undertaken with students and/or with the external community.   Finally, please outline the research directions you foresee pursuing in the College of Engineering, any cross-disciplinary and collaborative aspects, and the strategies you will take to address each direction. 

 Teaching statement (1 page): 
 Please summarize your past instructional and mentorship experiences, your pedagogical philosophy, your plans/goals for teaching in the College of Engineering (including existing and proposed courses), and your strategies for teaching and mentoring global student populations. 

   Leadership statement (1 page): 
 Please describe your past experiences and activities and/or your future plans detailing your leadership style, how you intend to cultivate a culture that promotes a sense of belonging, including fostering a free and open exchange of ideas and managing different perspectives to help others strengthen their practice. 

 Northeastern University is an equal opportunity employer, seeking to recruit and support a broadly diverse community of faculty and staff.  Northeastern values and celebrates diversity in all its forms and strives to foster an inclusive culture built on respect that affirms inter-group relations and builds cohesion.

 All qualified applicants are encouraged to apply and will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, religion, color, national origin, age, sex, sexual orientation, disability status, or any other characteristic protected by applicable law.
 
 Position Type 
 
Academic 
 Additional Information 
 
 Northeastern University considers factors such as candidate work experience, education and skills when extending an offer.  
 
 Northeastern has a comprehensive benefits package for benefit eligible employees. This includes medical, vision, dental, paid time off, tuition assistance, wellness & life, retirement- as well as commuting & transportation. Visit https://hr.northeastern.edu/benefits/ for more information.    
 




 All qualified applicants are encouraged to apply and will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, religion, color, national origin, age, sex, sexual orientation, disability status, or any other characteristic protected by applicable law.
 
 
 
 Pay Range: 
Assistant Professor: $118,000.00 - $137,000.00 | Associate Professor: $126,000.00 - $168,000.00 | Professor: $150,000.00 - $251,000.00 
 With the pay range(s) shown above, the starting salary will depend on several factors, which may include your education, experience, location, knowledge and expertise, and skills as well as a pay comparison to similarly-situated employees already in the role. Salary ranges are reviewed regularly and are subject to change.
